newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE SEEN RETURNING TO FALLS NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE SEEN RETURNING TO FALLS NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Polish shares are seen falling next week as investors return to profit-taking after the bourse's previous 100-percent surge this year, although some analysts say there is still a chance for further gains.

Analysts said a 4.9-percent gain during Wednesday and Thursday, leaving the main market flat for the week at 13,497.9 points, represented buying on the back of a 14.6-percent fall since October 9 that had made prices attractive.
That day the market hit a 30-month high at 15,078.7 points.
"It's seems a lot of large investors have left recently, and I don't think they're going to come back immediately," said Krzysztof Rogalski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Analysts put strong support at 12,300 points.

Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital & Investment, said recent big losses by firms such as Agros and Polifarb Wroclaw , traditionally popular among foreign investors, suggested foreign selling.

Analysts also said both foreign and domestic investors were worried by the lower house of parliament's surprise decision last week to cut taxes for lower earners, a step seen increasing the budget deficit and fuelling inflation.
"It doesn't bode well -- it suggests there's no continuity in political or economic policy," said Ryszard Sikora, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
But analysts said a good sign was that President Aleksander Kwasniewski was expected to reject the tax bill later in November if the upper house, the Senate, failed to block it.
Some analysts said the market had a chance to rise next week, seeing a good sign in the higher turnover that accompanied Thursday's gain.

"The higher turnover is a good sign...but stocks might be mixed on Monday because the market is usually not too dynamic after a long weekend," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Markets are closed on Friday for All Saints Day.
Analysts said the main market's biggest loser this week, Espebepe down 18.8 percent, was hurting after its president's statement last week that it might go bankrupt.
The stock surged 9.5 percent on Thursday in a speculative rebound, analysts said.

They said top gainer Animex , up 14.9 percent, was helped by a buy recommendation from Bank Handlowy SA brokerage and a newspaper report reminding investors that the firm had won tax refunds and would seek more.
